title: Chapter 8.  Environment, Green Spaces & Sukhna Lake

blocks.content: Chandigarh's environment chapter is unusual among Indian UTs — instead of forests and wildlife sanctuaries, the star topics here are deliberately engineered green infrastructure: the Leisure Valley, Sukhna Lake, and one of Asia's largest rose gardens, all direct products of Le Corbusier's original master plan.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Sukhna Lake is an artificial reservoir created in 1958 by damming the Sukhna Choe, a seasonal stream from the Shivalik Hills.
Le Corbusier designed the green infrastructure of Chandigarh, incorporating the continuous linear park network known as Leisure Valley.
Sukhna Lake and its catchment area in the Shivalik foothills are designated as an Eco-Sensitive Zone to prevent urban encroachment and siltation.
Urban environmental management in Chandigarh emphasizes maintaining high per capita green cover and protecting local biodiversity.

blocks.content: Sukhna Lake, in Sector 1, was created in 1958 by damming the seasonal Sukhna Choe stream flowing down from the Shivalik Hills — conceived by Le Corbusier as an essential recreational and aesthetic counterpart to the formal Capitol Complex nearby.

Sukhna Lake was notified as a wetland under the Wetland (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017 in 2019, and in September 2025 the Chandigarh State Wetland Authority approved a proposal to designate it as a Ramsar Site of International Importance — which, once finalised by the Ramsar Secretariat, would become Chandigarh's first Ramsar site. As of early 2026 the proposal had been cleared by the Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change and forwarded for final international designation, recognising the lake's ecological role as a habitat for migratory birds within the wider Shivalik foothill watershed — a live current-affairs fact for this UT worth verifying closer to your exam date.
Sukhna Lake was created in 1958 by damming the Sukhna Choe, a seasonal stream coming down from the Shivalik Hills.

Sukhna Lake is a globally cited example of successful sediment/silt management for an artificial reservoir, given continuous engineering efforts (including afforestation of the surrounding catchment) to prevent the lake from silting up from Shivalik runoff.

★ EXAM POINT: Sukhna Lake's Ramsar Site status is a live current-affairs-cum-environment fact for Chandigarh (proposal cleared, final designation pending as of early 2026) — always check the latest official Ramsar site count and Sukhna's status when this comes up, since the national list is updated frequently.
Green Infrastructure — Le Corbusier's Planned Green Network

cells: An 8-km chain of continuous parks and gardens threading through the city — Le Corbusier's designated 'lungs' of Chandigarh, connecting several sectors without a break
One of the largest rose gardens in Asia, with over a thousand varieties of roses; hosts the annual Rose Festival
Specialised horticultural garden showcasing native and ornamental plant collections
Terraced Garden / Garden of Fragrance / Garden of Palms
A series of themed gardens within the Leisure Valley network, each dedicated to a plant theme

A 40-acre sculpture garden built entirely from industrial and household waste material by self-taught artist Nek Chand Saini, begun secretly in 1957 and made public in 1976 — now a major heritage and tourism site (see Chapter 10)

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Chandigarh is frequently cited as one of India's greenest planned cities — a large share of its total area is under parks, gardens and tree cover by deliberate design, not accident, distinguishing it from organically grown cities where green cover is often an afterthought.

items: Sukhna Lake was declared a notified wetland under the Wetland (Conservation and Management) Rules.
The seasonal stream dammed to form Sukhna Lake is the Sukhna Choe originating in the Shivalik Hills.
Le Corbusier designed Leisure Valley as a continuous 8 km long green corridor passing through multiple sectors.

Chandigarh has consistently ranked among the top Indian cities in Swachh Survekshan (national cleanliness survey) rankings for its size category, reflecting sustained investment in solid-waste management and civic upkeep.
The UT has actively promoted solar rooftop adoption and was among the earlier Indian cities to push net-metering solar policy for residential and government buildings.

Rainwater harvesting is mandated for buildings above a certain plot size under Chandigarh's building bye-laws, part of a broader groundwater-conservation push given the region's declining water table.

Sukhna Lake (Sector 1) — created 1958 by damming the Sukhna Choe; notified as a protected wetland in 2019; Ramsar Site proposal approved by the State Wetland Authority in Sept 2025, final designation pending.
Leisure Valley — an 8-km unbroken green corridor of parks, Le Corbusier's 'lungs' of the city.
Zakir Hussain Rose Garden (Sector 16) — one of Asia's largest rose gardens, hosts the annual Rose Festival.
Nek Chand's Rock Garden (Sector 1) — 40-acre sculpture garden built from industrial/household waste, begun secretly in 1957, opened 1976.
Chandigarh ranks consistently high in Swachh Survekshan cleanliness rankings for its city-size category.
